div.div:
dătātim , adv. [dato),
I.giving in turn or reciprocally, "invicem dando," Non. 96, 15 (ante-class. and rare): isti qui ludunt datatim, i. e. (in playing ball) by tossing from one to the other, * Plaut. Curc. 2, 3, 17. Obscenè, Enn. ap. Isid. Orig. 1, 25, 2; Afran. and Pomp. ap. Non. 96, 19 (Afran. v. 222; Pomp. v. 1 ribbeck); cf. Nov. ap. Non. ib. (v. 23 Ribbeck).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
